newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei index plunges below key 19,000 level.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei index plunges below key 19,000 level.

text.p: The key index on the Tokyo stock market plunged below the important psychological level of 19,000 in Thursday afternoon trade for the first time in more than a year.
The benchmark Nikkei average of 225 leading shares briefly dropped to as low as 18,983.83, the first time it had been below the key 19,000 level since December 6, 1995.
Brokers said the current selloff was triggered last week by a lack of market confidence in the government's policies to prop up the economy.
The government has decided to end special income tax cuts from January and raise the consumption tax next April, sparking fears in the market that a fledgling recovery in the economy may be damaged.
The dollar's rise on Thursday in Tokyo trade also helped push stocks down by sparking fears over selling by foreign investors, brokers said.
On Thursday morning in Tokyo trade, the dollar rose above 115 yen, its highest level in over 44 months.
